name: @axf/core
description: AmberX Framework core — the runtime a peeled app inherits. Imports nothing of GizmoX, by construction.
//deps: React is a PEER dependency: core renders components but must never bundle its
own copy — two Reacts in one tree is the classic invalid-hook-call.
It is also a devDependency, purely so core can typecheck ON ITS OWN. It used
to resolve React by walking up into the GizmoX node_modules; that path
disappeared when the packages moved into pre-build, and relying on a parent
directory outside the package was never correct anyway.
@mui/material + @emotion/react + @emotion/styled were added to core on
2026-08-09 (axf-mui.bmpx P1), owner-authorised, and they REVERSE the rule
that stood here until that day. Core used to be MUI-free on the grounds
that the kit was an SDK convenience for ported GizmoX modules. The owner's
direction is the opposite: everything built from here on is MUI, so the
MUI theme is a CONTRACT of the framework, not a detail of one app. A theme
engine that cannot produce the theme object every surface consumes is not
driving the app — it is decorating it. `src/theme/mui.ts` is therefore in
core, and it cannot be written without importing createTheme.
They are PEERS for the same reason React is, and the failure mode is worse
rather than milder. Two @emotion/react copies means two style caches: the
provider from one copy is invisible to the styled() calls of the other, so
half the app renders unthemed with no error anywhere. Two @mui/material
copies means two ThemeContext identities, so core's ThemeProvider does not
reach studio's components. Both are silent — which is exactly why the
dependency is declared as a peer and never as a plain dependency.
Also devDependencies, on React's stated precedent: so core typechecks on
its own without resolving anything outside the package.
@mui/icons-material is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED here as it is in studio, and
check:imports NAMES it rather than leaving it to the dep-set message: every
icon resolves through the branding pack's --axf-brand-*/--gxb-* roles, and a
Material icon paints a shipped hex no theme can reach.
react-dom joined the peers on 2026-08-13, for `toolbar/inline.tsx`: an
inline toolbar placement is a real React bar portalled into an element the
app did not author, and createPortal lives in react-dom and nowhere else.
A PEER for the same reason React is — two react-dom copies is the same
invalid-hook-call, and portals from a second copy render into a tree the
first one does not reconcile. @types/react-dom is a devDependency on the
same precedent as @types/react: so core typechecks on its own.
@mui/material-nextjs is NOT here and must not be: it is App-Router
plumbing (SSR style flush + the cascade layer), so it belongs to studio,
which is the Next app. Core stays framework-agnostic and knows nothing
about a router.
